passage:
At the school activity fair, sign-up tables lined the hall. Dolma read every sheet twice. Poetry slam: what if she forgot the words? Debate: what if she was bad? Art contest: what if hers was the worst? She put her hands in her pockets and walked past all of them.
Anirban, holding a marker at the open-mic table, waved her over. "Try this one. Two minutes, four people, no marks."
"I'd probably mess up."
"Then you'll have messed up in front of four people. Not forty."
Dolma read four lines of a poem, her hands shaking. Nobody clapped loudly, but Anirban nodded, and her stomach unclenched. She took the marker and slowly wrote her name on the sheet for next week.

qa.q: How many people were at the open-mic table?
Why did Dolma walk past all the sign-up tables?
qa.a: She was afraid of failing: forgetting the words, being bad, being the worst, so she avoided anything she might fail at.

qa.q: What small step helped Dolma start?
qa.a: Trying a low-stakes attempt, two minutes in front of four people with no marks, made failing feel survivable.

qa.q: How does Anirban see Dolma's fear?
qa.a: Anirban sees it as small enough to face, and offers a low-stakes chance without judging her.

grounding: Dolma refuses to try things she might fail at; a low-stakes first attempt shows that fear of failure limits her more than failure would.
